definitionOfDone: Front render at the reference camera matches the chibi proportion lock: head+hair ~35% of figure height, goggles band at 63% of head height, fingertips at upper-thigh, crotch at ~36% of height from the ground.
Slime hair reads as blobby drooping teardrop locks with a rising crown tuft and falling droplets, never as a smooth helmet cap.
Goggles read as a single wide black glossy lens in a white rounded frame, wider than the head, with a black strap around the head and silver clips at the temples; small smile visible below.

Outfit palette reads turquoise-on-black: cropped boxy black jacket with turquoise piping and turquoise collar lining over a white tee, charcoal cargo joggers with turquoise outer-seam stripe, cargo pockets, gathered cuffs.
Backpack glass ink tank with turquoise liquid, black caps, silver bands, black harness straps with silver buckles, and a corrugated black hose looping to the right hip are visible from back/side/3-4.
Chunky sneakers with white midsole, turquoise outsole, black upper with turquoise panels and white laces.
Hierarchy is action-ready: articulated limbs/digits, hand_r blaster socket, back tank socket, detachable goggles/tank, colliders on macro parts.

actionReadiness.contract: Every macro/meso component should be generated as a stable named Object3D pivot node with a mesh child, action metadata, optional sockets, collider proxy, and destruction metadata.
requiredComponentFields: attachment for child appendages, connectors, limbs, tubes, handles, legs, horns, wings, branches, or cables
authoringRules: Do not collapse independently movable parts into one mesh.
Put transforms on component pivot groups, not only on raw meshes.
For attached child parts, put the pivot at the semantic root/socket and build visible geometry from localStart to localEnd.
Represent hinge, socket, detachable, and breakable intent even when no animation is implemented yet.
Use simplified collider proxies for runtime physics instead of visual mesh colliders by default.

destructionPolicy.fractureGroupNaming: Use stable semantic names such as body-shell, left-hinge, glass-panel, branch-segment.
destructionPolicy.debrisStrategy: Prefer detachable component groups and a small number of procedural fragments over random mesh explosion.

proceduralStrategy: Head: one ellipsoid volume; goggles = white ellipsoid body + black lens dome + flattened torus strap + metal clips.
Hair: hair-cap ellipsoid + 17 tapered-sweep locks with bulbous tips + crown tuft + teardrop droplets, standProud against the head.
Body: pelvis ellipsoid, abdomen/chest/neck/limb segments from attachment endpoints (bones), palms/digits as tapered sweeps.
Garments: tee = closed elliptical prism, jacket = C-section prism open at the front, collar = small C-ring; piping/stripes as vertexPaint regions.
Shoes: ellipsoid upper + extruded footprint midsole/outsole + lathe collar + micro tongue/panel/heel tab/lace bars, yawed 12 deg toe-out.
Backpack: box back plate + lathe glass/liquid/caps/valve + torus bands + corrugated tapered-sweep hose to the right hip.
Flat textureless toon-PBR materials with team-colour slots; no external textures.
animationAnchors: pelvis is the single bone root; spine abdomen->chest->neck->head; arms clavicle->upper-arm->forearm->hand->digits; legs thigh->shin->foot
hand-r socket 'hand_r' holds the blaster prop; back-plate socket 'back' holds the tank (detachable)
head socket 'goggles' (goggles detach for the swim form); root socket 'ground'
hair/goggles/tank/shoe parts ride their parent bone rigidly (hair is never smooth-skinned)
risks: Hair locks are inferred paths from silhouettes; lock topology must pass the silhouette review before material tuning.
Glass transmission on the tank costs an extra render pass in three.js; may fall back to opacity in optimization-pass.
Extruded jacket/tee prisms have straight sides; shoulder slope comes from the clavicle yokes and may need a lofted shell in form-refinement.
